In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Defender-in-Chief.

In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Army Protector.
The literal line makes the same 護軍/太尉 substitution; Army Protector is the correct rendering.
The given name 瑰 is Guī, not Méi; the heading romanization is a naming error.
The literal heading repeats the same false Méi reading of 瑰; Gui is required.
The Prince of Donghai’s body had been cremated by Shi Le; Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.
The Prince of Donghai, Yue, had already had his corpse burned by Shi Le; his consort Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.
The Chinese names 東海王越, marks the burning as already done with 既, and identifies 妃裴氏 as his consort; the repair restores those elements without changing the rest of the human wording.
Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Carefree Roaming and shedding ritual.

Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Zhuangzi’s Hao-river debates and shedding ritual.
虛詠濠肆 alludes to Zhuangzi’s Hao-river (濠) free talk, not the chapter title 逍遙遊; the replacement corrects the allusion.
You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and was as celebrated as his elder brother in youth.
You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and in youth was as celebrated as Gui.
少與瑰齊名 does name 瑰, so the kinship-only original is incomplete, but the proposal’s Mei repeats the false romanization of 瑰 already rejected at the heading.
In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser and kept him at Stone fortress.
In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser, and he accompanied Dao at Stone fortress.
隨導在石頭 makes Yuan Dan the one who accompanied Wang Dao at Stone fortress; “kept him” reverses the agency.

Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.

Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.”
The Chinese speech is a complete quoted utterance (謂將校曰「……」); closing the English quotation is required and changes no meaning.
Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—emotion overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.
Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—the grand consort’s unbounded grief overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.
此蓋太妃罔已之情 names the grand consort as the agent of the grief that broke burial law; omitting 太妃 leaves the emotion unattributed.
When Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.
When the heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.
會稽世子元顯 is the heir apparent; 會稽王 belongs to 道子 in the same sentence, so “Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji” is a title error.
Under Taiyuan the academy added a hundred students and named Yin their doctoral libationer.
During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as erudite of the National University.
領國子博士 is concurrent charge as National University erudite (博士), not 祭酒; “erudit” in the proposal is not English for that office.
His ancestor Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.
His grandfather Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.
祖融, paired with 父康 in the next sentence, is Yin Yi’s grandfather, not a vague ancestor.
His ancestor Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.
His grandfather Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.
The literal likewise renders 祖 as ancestor; grandfather is the kinship term required by 祖融.
Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s guard-general of the right.
Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s Guard General.
魏衛將軍肅 is Guard General; 右 is not in the Chinese, so “of the right” is invented.
